findings.message: The 'Resolve source workflow run ID' step defines `env:` twice; GitHub Actions rejects duplicate mapping keys, so the whole workflow file fails to load. On any workflow_run completion or manual dispatch, GitHub reports an invalid workflow file ('env' is already defined) and no job runs, so no remediation issue is ever created.

The run script has two `else` branches (the old fallback and the new same-week one), which is a bash syntax error. Bash parses the whole `if` before running any of it, so every path fails. Even the workflow_run path (`elif`) never runs. Bash fails with `syntax error near unexpected token else`, the step fails, and the run ID is never set.

Inside the `if` branches, the heredoc body and the `PY` terminator are indented 2 spaces past the block's base indentation. YAML keeps those spaces, so `<<'PY'` never finds a terminator at column 0, and the Python code starts with an unexpected indent. Even with the duplicate `else` fixed, manual dispatch without run_id either swallows the rest of the script into the heredoc or fails with a Python IndentationError, so the fallback lookup never works.

The issue step only runs when has_recommendations == 'true'. If a later scan has no fixable packages, the existing open issue is never updated or closed and keeps listing outdated recommendations. Week 1 creates an issue listing openssl -> 3.x. Week 2 is clean, so the step is skipped and the issue still tells maintainers to upgrade packages that are already fixed.

urllib follows the 302 from archive_download_url to blob storage and forwards the `Authorization: Bearer` header. Signed blob URLs commonly reject requests that also carry an Authorization header. The artifact download gets 400/403 AuthenticationFailed from the storage host after the redirect, and the step fails before building the report.

`${{ inputs.run_id }}` is pasted straight into the bash script, so a crafted dispatch input can run arbitrary shell commands in a job holding an issues:write token. A dispatcher passes run_id `1"; curl ... $GH_TOKEN; echo "` and the command runs with the token in the environment. It should go through an env var and be checked as numeric.

The workflow_run trigger accepts successful weekly-scan runs from any branch, but the fallback logic and the issue text assume pre-update-release. A successful scan run on a feature branch or PR overwrites the tracking issue with that branch's results.
